subsystems.name: Scoop vehicle
subsystems.role: flies through the outer atmosphere at hypersonic speed, compressing and capturing gas without burning up.

subsystems.name: Propulsion and power
subsystems.role: provides the thrust and energy to enter the atmosphere, climb back out and reach a rendezvous orbit.

subsystems.name: Separation plant
subsystems.role: separates hydrogen from helium and then helium-3 from helium-4 on board.

subsystems.name: Storage and transfer
subsystems.role: holds cryogenic liquids and hands them to a tanker or depot.

subsystems.name: Navigation and control
subsystems.role: works without a pilot, in a hostile radiation and thermal environment.

subsystems.name: Support infrastructure
subsystems.role: the in-system logistics that make repeat trips possible.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the atmosphere
buildSteps.detail: Probes and orbiters measure composition, winds and temperatures. The Galileo probe entered Jupiter's atmosphere in 1995; more measurements would be needed before mining could be planned.

buildSteps.title: Choose a harvest site
buildSteps.detail: Trade altitude, wind speed, turbulence and radiation dose — Jupiter's belts are brutal, so higher latitudes or Saturn may be safer.

buildSteps.title: Design the scoop
buildSteps.detail: Shape an inlet that compresses thin gas at many kilometres per second into a flow that can be cooled and liquefied, tested in shock tunnels and hypersonic wind tunnels.

buildSteps.title: Build the power plant
buildSteps.detail: A nuclear-thermal or fusion drive light enough to leave the gravity well, or a beamed-power alternative.

buildSteps.title: Build the separation plant
buildSteps.detail: Cryogenic distillation and isotope separation miniaturised to fit a spacecraft, using the extreme cold of the local environment to help.

buildSteps.title: Fly a robotic demonstrator
buildSteps.detail: A single uncrewed pass: skim, scoop, separate, climb to orbit and vent or store the product.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Repeat passes with a tanker, refuelling the scoop vehicle between runs.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a fuel depot
buildSteps.detail: Many vehicles feeding an orbital depot, supplying fusion fuel or propellant to ships further out.

prerequisites.why: without it there is no way to enter and leave a gas giant's gravity well while carrying a payload.
it is far harder to ignite than deuterium–tritium and would be pointless to mine before it works.

prerequisites.tech: Hypersonic scooping in a hydrogen atmosphere
prerequisites.why: gas has to be captured and decelerated at entry speeds of tens of kilometres per second without melting the vehicle.
separating and liquefying hydrogen and helium isotopes in flight has never been done at scale.
electronics and materials near a gas giant face particle doses far beyond near-Earth experience.

pathway.milestone: atmospheric probes and orbiter surveys of Jupiter and Saturn
pathway.unlocks: the composition data on which any resource case must rest.

pathway.milestone: robotic scoop demonstrator that captures gas and reaches orbit
pathway.unlocks: proof that the pass-and-climb cycle is physically workable.

pathway.milestone: orbital depot with repeat tanker runs
pathway.unlocks: a supply of propellant for deep-space transport, independent of Earth launch.

pathway.milestone: fuel exports from the outer solar system
pathway.unlocks: fusion fuel and propellant at a scale that could support large in-space infrastructure, if fusion power ever works.
